html:
The Bará, who call themselves Waípinõmakã, are a Tukanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, living on the upper Tiquié and Pirá-Paraná rivers.

Like the Desana, Tatuyo and Makuna around them, they marry outside their own language group, and they live in large communal longhouses called malocas. They grow manioc and fish. Little is published about their history apart from studies of their kinship and language.
